## Why

Each earlier issue added the coordinator's instructions for its own tools. Nobody had checked the whole prompt against the spec since. A gap check on 2026-11-04 did that: an agent compared technical spec sections 4.1, 4.2, 5.2, and 9 with the coordinator's view file (`src/agent/coordinator.view.md`). Of about 70 things the spec says the coordinator does, 64 were covered. This issue fixes the gaps it found, and three found earlier, so the recorded trips (#66, #67, #68) don't run into problems we already know about.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 4.2 and 5.2.
- [Functional spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/functional-spec.md), sections 1 and 2: the contiguous United States.

## Open questions

- ~~Are about two dozen tools too many for the coordinator? If it chooses badly, merge the add, update, and remove tools for each kind of item.~~ Moved to #53 on 2026-11-04, as the "tool use" general evaluator. Only recorded sessions can show whether the coordinator picks badly.
- ~~Do the instructions say clearly enough what the trip tools' "new or gone" check results mean? Today the prompt says only that each tool "replies with the feasibility check results the change made new or gone, anywhere in the trip." A tool reply then says, for example, "No new or gone check results." "Gone" means a result that was there before the change and isn't after it, such as a warning the change fixed, or one about a stop the change removed. Raised 2026-10-23, while checking the raw view from #125.~~ Moved to #252 on 2026-11-04. The fix changes how a write's reply is laid out, which is code, not only the instructions.
- ~~Should the instructions tell the coordinator not to describe its own steps to the user? On a new trip, its reply began "I need to read brief and memory first." That's a note to itself, written as reply text before its tool calls, so the user sees it as the reply's first line. Raised 2026-10-23, while checking #123.~~ Settled 2026-11-04 in chat: yes, it's in "Do". #53 also gets a general evaluator, "the reply is for the user", to show whether it still happens.
- ~~Does the "changed" mark on check results (#55) come back too often to be useful? A check result is changed when its text differs from the saved one (domain model 4.8). A daily driving warning's text names its day, such as "Day 4 needs about 4 h 8 m of driving." So adding or removing a stay before that day renumbers it, and the warning comes back changed, though nothing about it got worse. In #55's Moab chat on 2026-10-24, adding the Moab stay gave "Changed warning: The trip is 4 days, and the brief asks for 5" and "Changed warning: Day 4 needs about 4 h 8 m of driving." The coordinator stayed quiet about both, since the skeleton wasn't finished. If later runs show it raising renumbered warnings, compare the results without the day number, or leave the day number out of the text.~~ Dropped 2026-11-04 in chat. Nothing has shown it to be a problem. In the one chat that saw it, the coordinator stayed quiet.
- ~~Should the instructions say the app plans trips only in the contiguous United States? Functional spec sections 1 and 2 say so, and list Canada as out of scope, but neither the coordinator's instructions nor technical spec 5.2 says it. So going through 5.2 alone won't catch it. In Joe's session on the live site on 2026-10-28 (agent session `0f63f3da-4112-4943-93ec-af8fe6576296`), the coordinator offered to plan the Niagara stay on the Canadian side, and added a stay in Niagara Falls, Ontario. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-28.~~ Settled 2026-11-04 in chat: yes, it's in "Do".

## Do

Add each of these to the coordinator's instructions (`src/agent/coordinator-prompt.ts` and the files next to it), in the section it fits:

- **"What's left to decide?"** How to answer it, from technical spec 5.2: a whole read and trip memory, then the stops and lodging still empty or proposed, the open warnings, and the open items in trip memory. Mention approved exceptions briefly. Nothing in the instructions covers it today.
- **The contiguous United States only.** The app plans trips only there, as functional spec sections 1 and 2 say. Don't offer, or add, a stay or stop outside it, such as Niagara Falls, Ontario.
- **Replies are for the user.** Don't write notes to yourself as reply text, such as "I need to read brief and memory first."
- **A standing preference also goes to user memory,** even when the trip brief holds it for this trip. Technical spec 5.2, "Writing memory", has the rule and its example: "we never drive more than 5 hours, on any trip" sets comfortable driving hours, and is saved to user memory too. Today the Memory section has only the trip memory half of the rule: don't save to trip memory what the trip brief or the itinerary holds.
- **Stops the user chose decide their own part of the road.** If they're inland, the leg runs inland there, and the coordinator doesn't question it (technical spec 4.2, "The route preference is for the stretches nobody has decided"). The instructions cover only the waypoints half.
- **A stop whose purpose says how long:** when telling the user what it pushes later in the day, use the same rough timing as the worker brief (technical spec 5.2). Today the instructions don't tie the two together, so they could differ.

Also:

- Fix technical spec 4.2's step 4, "Fill". It says a stay researcher goes to a stay with "lodging not yet selected". Section 5.2, and the instructions, send one only for lodging with no candidates yet. 5.2 is right: lodging that already has candidates doesn't need another researcher. Change 4.2 to match.
- The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR.
- Run `npm run agent-views`, so the coordinator's view file shows the changes.

## Done when

- The PR description lists each item in "Do", with the part of the instructions that now covers it.
- `npm run check` passes.

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** the PR. Propose each answer in the PR's decisions comment, and Joe agrees by approving the PR.

They're evaluations now. #69 covers both, with acceptance scenario S7, "Resume and new session" (functional spec 11).

Moved from the [development plan](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/plan/development-plan.md#phase-32-finish-the-coordinators-instructions). Reworked on 2026-11-04, after the gap check. The real-agent tests for a new session's opening line and "what's left to decide?" came out. They're evaluations now. #69 covers both, with acceptance scenario S7, "Resume and new session" (functional spec 11).

**Starts** once #61, #62, and #64 are merged.

## Why

Each earlier issue added the coordinator's instructions for its own tools. This one checks that the instructions cover everything in technical spec sections 5.2 and 9, before whole trips are planned in #67 and #68.

## Design

- [Technical spec](https://github.com/nimbusscale/road-trip-agent/blob/main/design/technical-spec.md), sections 5.2 and 9.

## Open questions

- Are about two dozen tools too many for the coordinator? If it chooses badly, merge the add, update, and remove tools for each kind of item.
- Do the instructions say clearly enough what the trip tools' "new or gone" check results mean? Today the prompt says only that each tool "replies with the feasibility check results the change made new or gone, anywhere in the trip." A tool reply then says, for example, "No new or gone check results." "Gone" means a result that was there before the change and isn't after it, such as a warning the change fixed, or one about a stop the change removed. Raised 2026-10-23, while checking the raw view from #125.
- Should the instructions tell the coordinator not to describe its own steps to the user? On a new trip, its reply began "I need to read brief and memory first." That's a note to itself, written as reply text before its tool calls, so the user sees it as the reply's first line. Raised 2026-10-23, while checking #123.
- Does the "changed" mark on check results (#55) come back too often to be useful? A check result is changed when its text differs from the saved one (domain model 4.8). A daily driving warning's text names its day, such as "Day 4 needs about 4 h 8 m of driving." So adding or removing a stay before that day renumbers it, and the warning comes back changed, though nothing about it got worse. In #55's Moab chat on 2026-10-24, adding the Moab stay gave "Changed warning: The trip is 4 days, and the brief asks for 5" and "Changed warning: Day 4 needs about 4 h 8 m of driving." The coordinator stayed quiet about both, since the skeleton wasn't finished. If later runs show it raising renumbered warnings, compare the results without the day number, or leave the day number out of the text.
- Should the instructions say the app plans trips only in the contiguous United States? Functional spec sections 1 and 2 say so, and list Canada as out of scope, but neither the coordinator's instructions nor technical spec 5.2 says it. So going through 5.2 alone won't catch it. In Joe's session on the live site on 2026-10-28 (agent session `0f63f3da-4112-4943-93ec-af8fe6576296`), the coordinator offered to plan the Niagara stay on the Canadian side, and added a stay in Niagara Falls, Ontario. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-28.

## Do

- Go through every item in technical spec sections 5.2 and 9, and make sure the instructions cover it. Add what's missing, such as the opening line of a new session and "what's left to decide?"

## Done when

- The PR description lists each item in sections 5.2 and 9, with the part of the instructions that covers it.
- Real-agent tests (DEVELOPMENT.md section 5) pass for a new session's opening line and for "what's left to decide?"

## Ends in

A PR.

**Settled in:** chat. Propose each answer to Joe in chat first, and write it in once he agrees.

## Do

- Go through every item in technical spec sections 5.2 and 9, and make sure the instructions cover it. Add what's missing, such as the opening line of a new session and "what's left to decide?"

- Have the coordinator ask its first-turn questions in a better order: first the few it needs to offer the trip sketches, and the rest later. In Joe's Bar Harbor session on the live site on 2026-10-30 (agent session `89f4dea6-6cb9-4320-a917-c063620acca9`), its first reply asked 7 numbered questions, though the instructions say "Ask a few questions at a time." Joe answered the ones the sketches needed, and the sketches in turn 2 came out well. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-30.

- Have each trip sketch say why each town on its path fits this user, not only why the sketch as a whole does. In the same Bar Harbor session, turn 2, Camden was in both sketches, and the only reason given was "one of Maine's prettiest harbor towns." Joe rated the turn down: "Route includes stay or stop in Camden, but doesn't mention why we would consider it. hard to choose the two options it laid out since we don't know anything about Camden." The instructions ask for "a few sentences on why someone would pick it", which the model read as a line per sketch. The implementer drafts the wording, and Joe reviews it in the PR. Raised by Joe on 2026-10-30.

The coordinator stayed quiet about both, since the skeleton wasn't finished. If later runs show it raising renumbered warnings, compare the results without the day number, or leave the day number out of the text.
